low_traffic.description: Very light load (~3 req/s) on four healthy servers.

normal_traffic.description: Steady 10 req/s, mixed low/medium backends (the original comparison setup).

spike_traffic.description: Mostly quiet with sharp random request spikes.

ramp_up.description: Request rate climbs linearly from 1 to ~24 req/s.

flash_crowd.description: Registration-rush flash crowd: sustained ~36 req/s on healthy servers (herding test).

slow_server.description: server1 becomes slow (250 ms base latency).

single_overload.description: server1 overloaded (92% CPU, 420 MB, capacity 4, 15% errors).

double_overload.description: server1 and server3 overloaded at the same time.

queue_buildup_high_traffic.description: server4 has tiny capacity (3) while traffic is high - queues build up.

heterogeneous_servers.description: One idle, one low, one medium and one high-load server.

spike_during_overload.description: Request spikes arrive while server2 is overloaded.

hard_failure.description: server2 hard-fails (fast 90% error responses - a 'black hole').

flapping_server.description: server1 flips between overloaded and healthy every 6 s.

cascading_degradation.description: Servers degrade one after another (slow -> overload -> queue buildup).

overload_migration.description: The hotspot moves: server1 overloaded, then server4 instead.

policy_probes.note: Synthetic snapshots built with value ranges calibrated to the real backend presets; a decision is correct when the chosen server is healthy/busy-but-healthy, never degraded or failed.
